claude.rationale: The deal transferred only a block of minority equity (613,888,888 Yahoo Japan shares via SoftBank tender offer) plus termination of the 1996 JV governance arrangement and board-seat withdrawal; the registrant explicitly held no operating business, workforce, or operational processes of Yahoo Japan (those were run by Yahoo Japan itself). Because no product-producing processes (T5) or organization/people (T6) belonged to the registrant, there is no product-vs-process (gap_45) or process-vs-people (gap_56) mismatch to code — what crossed was a governance/equity position only. Retained transitional consent and access rights for up to 12 months are documented but pertain to shareholding, not to any operating substrate transfer, so both gaps are 0.

gemini.rationale: The registrant, Altaba Inc., is a closed-end management investment company holding minority equity positions with no operating business, workforce, or operational processes. Because there are no products, processes, or organizations being transferred (T4, T5, and T6 are null), there are no structural mismatches or gaps between these tiers at closing.

grok.rationale: The N-CSR states the registrant held only equity positions and governance rights in Yahoo Japan; operating businesses, workforces, and processes belonged to Yahoo Japan, not the registrant. The 8-K closing structure transfers a block of shares via SoftBank tender, terminates the JV Agreement, and withdraws board designees, with only transitional consent/access rights retained—no customer-facing product (T4) and no operational processes (T5) crossed, so gap_45=0; likewise no processes or organization/people (T6) transferred, so gap_56=0.
